elbow_flex.source: Gravitus Incline Chest Press: "Press to near full extension without completely locking out the elbows, which maintains tension on the chest" (illustrative 15 degrees); the bent start at the chest is illustrative at 90 degrees, matching a loaded machine start

shrug_cm.source: Gravitus Incline Chest Press: "Allowing the shoulders to rise toward the ears, particularly during the pressing phase, which can reduce chest activation"

torso_lean.source: Gravitus Incline Chest Press: "Excessively arching the lower back during the pressing movement, which can reduce chest engagement and potentially create lower back stress"

muscles.peakSource: Gravitus Incline Chest Press: pressing to near full extension without locking out "maintains tension on the chest," so effort is highest approaching that near-top position

mistake.name: Shrug and arch

tells.text: The shoulders rise toward the ears through the press.
The lower back arches off the pad to help finish the press.

mistake.source: Gravitus Incline Chest Press: "Allowing the shoulders to rise toward the ears... can reduce chest activation"; "Excessively arching the lower back during the pressing movement... can reduce chest engagement and potentially create lower back stress"

sources: Contact fact (backrest angle, unverified_on_machine): Gravitus gives "typically 30-45 degrees" as the setup range, a real-world angle, not this app's `bench` setting unit, so it is not written into `machine.settings` here; the owner's gym checklist confirms the actual rig value
